name: Applied Audio Products Inc.
dirt_evidence: Applied Fuzz & Treble Booster; Big Fuzz; Goya fuzzes; Guild FW-3 and other OEM dirt
notes: Applied is explicitly identified by specialist research as a physical U.S. pedal manufacturer. A 1968 city directory lists Applied Audio Products Inc. as an amplifier manufacturer at 111 Market St., Kenilworth, NJ, while historical research documents its effects production and OEM work. Preserve Goya, Guild, Lou Rose, Crown and other customer labels as separate marketed entities.

name: United Musical Industries (UMI)
dirt_evidence: UMI Buzz Tone & Volume Expander; other UMI effects
notes: UMI is documented as United Musical Instruments and as a physical U.S. manufacturer of the late-1960s Buzz Tone & Volume Expander. A Gearphoria historical feature identifies founder Richard Soloway and states UMI made pedals; specialist Kimberly research places UMI later in the production chain. Preserve Apollo, Conrad and other marketed labels as related products rather than duplicate makers.

name: LIMMCO / Long Island Musical Merchandise Co.
entity_type: Historical distributor with documented in-house micro-manufacture
dirt_evidence: Kimberly Buzz Box and Volume Expander v1
notes: LIMMCO was principally a wholesaler/distributor, but its owner Bob Seidman is reported to have said the first Kimberly Buzz Box and Volume Expander units were initially made in LIMMCO's Long Island warehouse before production was outsourced. Include as a manufacturing entity only for this documented initial batch, never as a broad pedal-company catalog.
